parties.licensor: The supplier (the user who uploads, lists, collects or delivers dataset materials); suppliers retain ownership and buyers receive only the licence stated in the transaction terms
parties.licensee: The buyer, with end clients and their service providers able to use materials under the transaction terms; truelabel itself takes a sublicensable operating licence
parties.operator_role: venue (truelabel says it is not a party to the buyer-supplier contract unless a separate written agreement says otherwise; but data licences are also said to be governed by a truelabel MSA and Order, so truelabel may be contracting party on managed deals)

permitted_use.value: Set per transaction: buyers may use materials only within the licence, restrictions and permitted-use language of the accepted request, listing, order or SOW; they get only that licence and a purchase transfers nothing broader by default.

ai_training_rights.value: Buyers, end clients and their service providers may train, evaluate, validate, build, improve or commercialise AI/ML models and datasets only to the extent the transaction terms allow (no default grant); fine-tuning is named only as a buyer purpose. truelabel itself does not train foundation or unrelated commercial models on private materials unless an order, agreement or product setting authorises it, but may use aggregated/de-identified/operational derived data to improve its own service.

derivatives_and_model_outputs.value: No clause on ownership of trained models or model outputs; buyers may 'commercialize' models only as transaction terms allow, and by default must not deploy trained models in safety-critical physical systems without validation and human oversight.

sublicensing.value: Suppliers grant truelabel a sublicensable, non-exclusive, worldwide licence used to pass content to buyers, end clients and service providers; buyers may not resell raw materials by default, while end clients and service providers may use them under the transaction terms.

exclusivity.value: Only the supplier-to-truelabel platform licence is stated (non-exclusive); buyer exclusivity is neither offered nor excluded and would sit in the transaction terms.

warranties_by_provider.value: Suppliers/contributors represent they own or control all needed rights, must accurately describe provenance, collection conditions, consent status and limitations, and keep supporting records for buyer due diligence; truelabel gives no dataset warranty (as-is, no title/non-infringement) and says its review does not validate rights.

consent_and_release_warranty.value: The supplier (whoever uploads, collects or delivers) represents it holds all consents and releases for the advertised uses, expressly including AI/ML training by truelabel, buyers and end clients and covering likenesses, voices, biometrics and location; individual contributors may be asked to attest. Truelabel does not verify, and restricted categories (children, biometrics, health) are barred unless the order permits. Consent evidence goes to buyers only 'when required' by due diligence.

indemnity.value: One-way and uncapped in the text: every user (buyer or supplier) indemnifies truelabel for its use, its dataset materials, infringement, failure to obtain consents or releases, and downstream use; truelabel gives no indemnity and no buyer-supplier indemnity is stated.

liability_cap.value: truelabel's service liability is capped at the greater of fees paid for the specific transaction in the prior three months or USD 100, with consequential and model-performance losses excluded; for licensed data the (unpublished) truelabel MSA and Order govern warranties and liability instead.

payment_and_revenue_share.value: No rates published in the Terms: fees, commissions, payout timing and refund rules are disclosed in-product or in transaction terms; payments run through third-party processors and truelabel disclaims being an escrow agent or fiduciary.

deletion_on_termination.value: No deletion obligation on buyers: termination preserves licence restrictions and confidentiality but also 'rights already granted under completed transactions'.

takedown_and_erasure.value: truelabel may suspend or remove files and listings for a rights concern or legal risk, but nothing requires buyers to delete copies already delivered; rights granted under completed transactions survive termination, so buyers keep what they hold.

prohibited_uses.value: Default buyer bans (overridable by transaction terms): re-identifying individuals, extracting biometric identifiers, removing provenance or licence notices, reselling raw materials, combining against consent or privacy restrictions, unlawful surveillance, and deploying trained models in safety-critical systems without validation and oversight.

field_of_use.value: Defined per transaction through the request's licence scope and usage restrictions; restricted data categories need express order permission.

governing_law.value: Laws of the Emirate of Dubai and applicable UAE federal law; exclusive jurisdiction of Dubai courts over truelabel FZCO, unless a separate written agreement says otherwise.

change_of_terms.value: truelabel may update the Terms; material changes are posted on the page and, where appropriate, notified in-product or by email, with no notice period; continued use is acceptance.

unknowns.note: Section 16 hands warranties, disclaimers and liability for licensed data to a 'truelabel Master Services Agreement' and Order; no public copy was found at guessed URLs and none is linked from the Terms or footer.
No clause on whether a buyer can obtain exclusive rights to a listed or commissioned dataset.
No mechanism to pass a data subject's erasure request or a takedown to buyers who already hold copies, nor to models already trained.
Suppliers keep consent records and produce them on buyer due diligence; the Terms do not say consent or release documents are delivered with the data.
Silent on whether data collected against a buyer's request may later be listed and sold to others (channel conflict).
The Terms do not describe delivery into the buyer's own storage; they only mention integrations with storage and dataset-hosting tools and disclaim third-party services.
Commission and fee rates are 'disclosed in-product or in the applicable transaction terms', not in the Terms.
No supplier or truelabel right to audit buyer use of licensed data.
